summary: Attacked part 3 of the Curves, abelian varieties and Shimura varieties area — ModularCurvesPartII, SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCases, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/BelyiMaps, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves: 5 roadmaps, 111 stages, only 4 paper routes. One finding, high: twelve roadmaps depend on the 58-stage ModularCurves roadmap and refer to it only as '#81', a pull-request number that appears nowhere in the roadmap itself; not one of the twelve declares it as a prerequisite, and it records no consumers, so the dependency of a fifth of the atlas's arithmetic-geometry roadmaps on it is invisible in every machine-readable field. Its two siblings in this same area use those fields correctly, which is what makes this an omission rather than a convention.
checked: All 111 stages of the five roadmaps — ModularCurves 58, ModularCurvesPartII 20, BelyiMaps 15, EllipticCurves 12, SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCases 6 — with their titles, dependencies and the accepted audit verdict for each: 36 partly built, 72 not built, 3 process. This part has far more library support than parts 1 and 2 (EllipticCurves 8 of 12 partly built, ModularCurves 21 of 58, BelyiMaps 6 of 15), as expected for classical material.
Eligibility, measured rather than assumed: none of the papers this session has reviewed routes into this part, checked at route granularity across all 207 paper result files.

The four paper routes, which is too few for the omissions head that carried parts 1 and 2 — 4 routes across 111 stages, all into ModularCurvesPartII. So the weight of this red team fell on the dependency and library-boundary heads instead, and I say so rather than presenting a thin omissions pass as a clean one.

The identity of '#81', established before relying on it, since the whole finding turns on it. ModularCurvesPartII refers to its parent exclusively as '#81' — 14 times in its record, 23 including PR81 — and never once by roadmap name or id. The ModularCurves roadmap itself never uses the string. I matched them on content instead. ModularCurvesPartII's summary says 'Use #81's actual affine Y_1(N), Y_full(N), fixed-pairing Y(N,zeta) and Y(rho)' and 'Its Layer 10 compactifies only Y_H'; ModularCurves' Layer 5 is exactly '5a-tate-normal-form-and-y1n', '5b-full-ordered-bases-and-fixed-pairing' and '5c-the-twisted-curve-yrho', and its Layer 10 is 'layer-10-compactified-coarse-curves-over-Z1n-cusps-and-the-shimura-covering'. ShimuraVarieties:V8 pairs the two names directly, citing 'M4 and ModularCurves #81 for the examples' and 'PR81 Layer 10 supplies only prime N>=5 diamond quotients'. The layer numbering, the named curves and the compactification scope all agree, so #81 is tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves.

The internal calibration that makes the finding a finding rather than a house style, which is available inside this very area. Of the three tauceti-origin, `active` roadmaps here, two use the `consumers` field accurately: EllipticCurves is cited by exactly one roadmap in either directory, WeilConjectures, and declares exactly `consumers: ['WeilConjectures']`; BelyiMaps is cited by none and declares none. ModularCurves is cited by twelve and declares none. Same origin, same lifecycle, same field, opposite behaviour.

Whether the twelve are really consumers rather than incidental mentions. Each reference is to ModularCurves' own content: ModularCurvesPartII builds on its curves and compactification, ShimuraVarieties:V8 consumes '#81 Layer 10' and the row-basis dictionary for its modular-curve comparison, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A5 requires agreement 'with #81's actual elliptic scheme, differential, and pairing' for genus one, and ShimuraCompactifications, PELModuli, PerfectoidShimuraVarieties, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory, EllipticCurveModularity, ComplexComparisonPartII, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations, AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry and AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights each cite it once.

The dependency bookkeeping of the two campaign roadmaps here, which is otherwise clean: ModularCurvesPartII declares nine prerequisites and 19 consumers, SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCases six and one, and for both the set of roadmaps reached by a cross-roadmap stage `requires` edge is contained in the declared prerequisites. The nine include tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms, so ModularCurvesPartII does declare tauceti-origin prerequisites where it names them by id — which is precisely why the omission of its own parent stands out.

The library boundary, the head that could yield here because unlike parts 1 and 2 this material is classical and substantially built. The three tauceti roadmaps' verdicts are monotone with their content — EllipticCurves 8 of 12 partly built with 4 not built, ModularCurves 21 partly and 37 not, BelyiMaps 6 partly, 8 not, 1 process — and no stage I read instructs construction of something an audit records as built. ModularCurves' summary names its source discipline explicitly ('following N. Katz and B. Mazur, Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves ... The book is abbreviated KM, and its result numbering is used throughout'), and its Layer 0 is openly a prerequisites layer of scheme-theoretic inputs rather than a re-derivation.

Library trees, with sizes printed beside every result after two wrong paths produced false cleans earlier in this session: a full Mathlib checkout of 8556 .lean files and the Tau Ceti library tree of 5268.

findings.where: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves (its `consumers` field), and the `prerequisites` field of the twelve roadmaps that depend on it, beginning with ModularCurvesPartII
findings.claim: Twelve roadmaps depend on the 58-stage ModularCurves roadmap, and the dependency is recorded nowhere. Every one of them refers to it as '#81', a pull-request number that does not appear anywhere in the ModularCurves record, so the reference cannot be resolved to a roadmap from the atlas at all; none of the twelve declares tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves in its `prerequisites`; and ModularCurves declares `consumers: []`. The most striking case is ModularCurvesPartII, which is that roadmap's own Part II: it refers to '#81' 23 times, declares nine prerequisites including two other tauceti-origin roadmaps by id, and does not declare its parent. Any consumer computing the atlas's dependency graph therefore sees a 58-stage active roadmap that nothing depends on, and a Part II that does not depend on its Part I.
findings.evidence: #81 is tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves, matched on content because the string appears in neither direction. ModularCurvesPartII's summary: 'Identify the algebraic modular curves of #81 with the analytic modular curves already used by ModularForms and FuchsianOrbifolds ... Use #81's actual affine Y_1(N), Y_full(N), fixed-pairing Y(N,zeta) and Y(rho). Its Layer 10 compactifies only Y_H'. ModularCurves' stage slugs include '5a-tate-normal-form-and-y1n', '5b-full-ordered-bases-and-fixed-pairing', '5c-the-twisted-curve-yrho' and 'layer-10-compactified-coarse-curves-over-Z1n-cusps-and-the-shimura-covering'. ShimuraVarieties:V8 pairs name and number: 'M4 and ModularCurves #81 for the examples', 'the dictionary between row-basis actions in #81 and the adelic convention', and 'PR81 Layer 10 supplies only prime N>=5 diamond quotients with H<=(Z/N)x/{+-1}'. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A5 requires, for genus one, 'agreement with #81's actual elliptic scheme, differential, and pairing'. The twelve roadmaps referencing #81 or PR81, with reference counts: ModularCurvesPartII 23, ShimuraVarieties 4, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli 3, and one each for ShimuraCompactifications, PerfectoidShimuraVarieties, PELModuli, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory, EllipticCurveModularity, ComplexComparisonPartII, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations, AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry and AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights — 39 references in all. I checked each one's `prerequisites`: none declares tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves, though their declared prerequisite counts run from 1 to 12. tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_ModularCurves.json has `prerequisites: []` and `consumers: []` with lifecycle `active`. The calibration is internal to this area and leaves no room for a house-style explanation: of the three tauceti-origin active roadmaps here, EllipticCurves is cited by exactly one roadmap, WeilConjectures, and declares exactly `consumers: ['WeilConjectures']`; BelyiMaps is cited by none and declares none; ModularCurves is cited by twelve and declares none.
findings.fix: Two changes, and the first matters more than the bookkeeping. (1) Give the reference a resolvable form. Replace '#81' and 'PR81' with the roadmap id tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves, keeping the PR number only as a parenthetical provenance note, and cite layers by their slugs (for example 'layer-10-compactified-coarse-curves-over-Z1n-cusps-and-the-shimura-covering' rather than '#81 Layer 10'). At present a reader or tool that meets '#81' has no way to resolve it, which is why twelve unrecorded dependencies accumulated without being noticed. (2) Record the relation on both sides, as this area already does for EllipticCurves and WeilConjectures: add tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves to the `prerequisites` of the twelve, starting with ModularCurvesPartII, and add those twelve to ModularCurves' `consumers`. ModularCurvesPartII is the urgent one, since a Part II that does not depend on its Part I will be scheduled wrongly by any build-order consumer. No cycle is introduced: ModularCurves declares no prerequisites, so it is a source in the graph.
